recipe.title: Dal Tadka (Restaurant Style)

ingredients.name: green chilies (or serrano peppers - chopped or slit lengthwise)
light cream (or low fat cream, optional)
garlic cloves (- finely chopped, small to medium-sized)
dry red chilies (- broken and seeds removed)
kasuri methi (- crushed, (dry fenugreek leaves), optional)
kashmiri chilli powder (or cayenne pepper or paprika)

steps.text: Thoroughly rinse tuvar dal (tur dal) in water. Add them to a 3-litre stovetop pressure cooker. (You can also cook the lentils in a pot; if cooking in a pot soak for an hour or two and use about 3 to 3.5 cups water.)
steps.label: Prepare lentils

steps.text: Add the chopped onions, finely chopped tomatoes, chopped green chillies and finely chopped ginger to the pressure cooker with the dal.
steps.label: Add aromatics
consumes_ingredients: green chilies (or serrano peppers - chopped or slit lengthwise)

steps.text: Pour 2.5 cups of water into the pressure cooker.
steps.label: Add water

steps.text: Add turmeric powder and asafoetida (hing). Mix well.
steps.label: Season dal

steps.text: Pressure cook the lentils on medium to medium-high heat for about 7 to 8 whistles (about 8 to 10 minutes), or until the lentils become soft and creamy.
steps.label: Pressure cook
steps.attention_cue: Let the pressure drop naturally in the cooker and then only open the lid.
steps.doneness_cue: until the lentils become soft and creamy

steps.text: Let the pressure drop naturally in the cooker and then only open the lid. Check the lentils to see if they have cooked thoroughly and softened.
steps.label: Release pressure
steps.attention_cue: Let the pressure drop naturally in the cooker and then only open the lid.
steps.doneness_cue: check the lentils to see if they have cooked thoroughly and softened

steps.text: Mash the cooked lentils with a wired whisk or with a spoon and set aside.
steps.label: Mash dal

steps.text: If the consistency looks thick, add about ½ to 1 cup water to get a medium consistency. Mix again and on a low to medium-low heat simmer dal for 3 to 4 minutes.
steps.label: Adjust consistency

steps.text: Once the desired consistency is reached, add the light cream or low-fat cream (optional), garam masala powder, chopped coriander leaves (cilantro) and salt to taste. Turn off the heat.
steps.label: Finish dal
consumes_ingredients: light cream (or low fat cream, optional)

steps.text: To get the smoky flavor using the dhungar method (optional): using tongs, place a small piece of natural charcoal on a grill pan and burn until red hot. (This is optional — you can proceed directly to tempering.)
steps.label: Heat charcoal

steps.text: Place the red hot charcoal in a small steel bowl (or use a halved hollow onion instead of the bowl).
steps.label: Set charcoal

steps.text: Pour about ¼ teaspoon of oil or ghee on the charcoal. You will see fumes emanating as soon as you pour oil or ghee on the hot charcoal.
steps.label: Pour oil on charcoal

steps.text: Place this bowl on the dal, cover the cooker or pot with a lid and let the dal get infused. Only smoke for 1 to 2 minutes. Remove the bowl carefully with tongs and cover the cooker; set aside.
steps.label: Smoke dal

steps.text: Heat oil or ghee in a small pan over low or medium-low heat for the tempering (tadka).
steps.label: Heat oil

steps.text: Add the cumin seeds and crackle them until fried but not burnt.
steps.label: Crackle cumin

steps.text: Add the dry red chilies, asafoetida, and finely chopped garlic. Let the garlic brown lightly and the red chilies change color. Do not burn the garlic.
steps.label: Fry garlic
consumes_ingredients: dry red chilies (- broken and seeds removed)
garlic cloves (- finely chopped, small to medium-sized)
steps.doneness_cue: Let the garlic brown lightly and the red chilies change color

steps.text: Add the crushed kasuri methi and kashmiri red chili powder (or cayenne). Mix well and turn off the stove.
steps.label: Finish tempering
consumes_ingredients: kasuri methi (- crushed, (dry fenugreek leaves), optional)
kashmiri chilli powder (or cayenne pepper or paprika)

steps.text: Pour entire tempering mixture along with the oil or ghee into the prepared dal.
steps.label: Add tadka

steps.text: You can either mix the dal with tempering, or serve the dal tadka with the tempering on top of it.
steps.label: Serve options

steps.text: Garnish with coriander leaves.
steps.label: Garnish

steps.text: Serve Dal Tadka hot with steamed basmati rice or jeera rice, or enjoy with roti or paratha.
steps.label: Serve

notes: Method and steps taken from linked recipe structured data (vegrecipesofindia.com). I preserved optional/alternative cues exactly as given (dhungar method marked optional). Attention/duration cues quoted from source where present (pressure cooking, simmer, smoke). Ingredient names reproduced verbatim from the recipeIngredient list.
